questions.q: In the MITRE ATT&CK framework, what does a "tactic" represent?
options: The specific tool the red team used to execute an action
The attacker's goal at a given stage, such as Privilege Escalation or Exfiltration
The name of the blue team's detection rule
The dollar value of damage an attack could cause
questions.explain: ATT&CK organizes around 14 tactics, each representing the attacker's goal at a stage of the attack — techniques are the specific methods used to accomplish that goal.

questions.q: What is the relationship between T1059 and T1059.001 in ATT&CK?
options: T1059.001 is an older, deprecated version of T1059
They are unrelated techniques that happen to share a numbering coincidence
T1059 is Command and Scripting Interpreter; T1059.001 is a sub-technique of it, specifically PowerShell
T1059 is a tactic and T1059.001 is the tool used to detect it
questions.explain: T1059 is the broader technique (Command and Scripting Interpreter) and T1059.001 is one of its specific sub-techniques (PowerShell).

questions.q: Why does this lesson say red should announce a technique by its ATT&CK ID rather than a plain-language description during a purple team exercise?
options: ATT&CK IDs are required by law for any authorized penetration test
Plain language descriptions are always factually inaccurate
Blue's detection coverage matrix is organized by the same IDs, so an ID lets blue instantly check for the exact relevant rule rather than guessing
ATT&CK IDs take less time to type than a description
questions.explain: Because blue's own coverage matrix is organized by ATT&CK ID, announcing the same ID removes ambiguity about which specific detection should be checked.

questions.q: What does the MITRE ATT&CK Navigator actually do, as described in this lesson?
options: It automatically writes new SIEM detection rules without human input
It executes attacker techniques against a target environment automatically
It replaces the need for a scribe or facilitator during an exercise
It renders the ATT&CK matrix as a color-codable grid, letting a team visualize coverage as a heat map
questions.explain: The Navigator is a visualization tool — it turns a list of tested technique IDs into a color-coded heat map of detected, partially detected, and undetected coverage across the matrix.

questions.q: Why does mapping purple team results to ATT&CK IDs let a team compare their coverage against a specific real adversary?
options: Because ATT&CK catalogs known threat groups and the specific technique IDs they've been observed using, enabling a direct comparison
Because ATT&CK IDs are unique to each individual organization
Because every organization is assigned a single ATT&CK ID representing its total risk score
Because the Navigator tool automatically identifies which group attacked you
questions.explain: ATT&CK's group pages document specific technique sets observed from real threat actors, so mapping your own results to the same IDs enables a direct, meaningful comparison.
